sentences.zh: 自西漢有外戚之禍，歷代鑒之，崇爵厚祿，不畀事權，然而一失其馭，猶有肺附之變焉。

translations.literal: Since the Western Han there has been the calamity of imperial consort kin; successive dynasties took warning from it, granting lofty ranks and rich stipends but not conferring governing power; yet once control was lost, there were still changes like lung-and-liver attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Western Han, the power of imperial consorts' families has brought disaster; each dynasty took warning, granting lofty titles and rich stipends but withholding real authority—yet once control slipped, calamities still erupted like disease clinging to vital organs.

sentences.zh: 宋法待外戚厚，其間有文武才諝，皆擢而用之；

translations.literal: The Song law treats imperial consort kin generously; among them those with civil or military talent are all selected and employed;
translations.idiomatic: Under Song law, imperial consort kin were treated generously; those with civil or military talent were promoted and put to use;

sentences.zh: 怙勢犯法，繩以重刑，亦不少貸。

translations.literal: those who relied on influence and violated the law were bound with heavy punishment, and were not lightly spared.
translations.idiomatic: those who abused their position and broke the law were punished severely, without leniency.

sentences.zh: 仁、英、哲三朝，母後臨朝聽政，而終無外家幹政之患，將法度之嚴，體統之正，有以防閑其過歟？

translations.literal: In the three reigns of Renzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong, empresses dowager held court and heard government, yet in the end there was no trouble of the maternal clan interfering in politics—was it because the laws were strict and the institutional norms correct, so as to guard against their excesses?
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Renzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong, empresses dowager ruled from behind the screen, yet the maternal clans never seized power—was this because strict laws and proper institutions kept them in check?

sentences.zh: 抑母後之賢，自有以制其戚裏歟？

translations.literal: Or was it because the empresses dowager were worthy, and themselves had means to restrain their consort kin?
translations.idiomatic: Or because the empresses dowager were wise enough to restrain their own families?

sentences.zh: 作《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore 《Biographies of Imperial Consort Kin》 was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this chapter, 《Biographies of Imperial Consort Kin》.

sentences.zh: 杜審琦，定州安喜人，昭憲皇太后之兄。

translations.literal: Du Shenqi, a native of Anxi in Ding Prefecture, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenqi, of Anxi in Ding Prefecture, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian.

sentences.zh: 太后昆仲五人，審琦最長，其次審玉，次審瓊，次審肇，次審進。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had five brothers and sisters; Shenqi was eldest, next Shenyu, then Shen Qiong, Shen Zhao, and Shen Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had five siblings: Shenqi was the eldest, followed by Shenyu, Shen Qiong, Shen Zhao, and Shen Jin.

sentences.zh: 世居常山，以積善聞。

translations.literal: The family had long lived in Changshan and was known for accumulated goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long lived in Changshan and was known for its virtue.

sentences.zh: 審琦仕後唐，為義軍指揮使，天成二年卒，年三十五，審玉前一年卒，年二十二。

translations.literal: Shenqi served the Later Tang as commander of the Yijun army; he died in the second year of Tiancheng, aged thirty-five. Shenyu had died the year before, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi served the Later Tang as commander of the Yijun army and died in Tiancheng year 2 (927), aged thirty-five. Shenyu had died the year before, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 太祖開國，贈審琦左神武軍大將軍，以其子彥超為西京作坊使。

translations.literal: When Taizu founded the state, he posthumously awarded Shenqi Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army and appointed his son Yanchao as commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty, Taizu posthumously made Shenqi Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army and appointed his son Yanchao commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 彥超卒，贈左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Yanchao died, he was posthumously awarded Grand General of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchao died, he was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 審瓊，建隆初，授檢校國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Shen Qiong, at the beginning of Jianlong, was appointed acting Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qiong: at the start of Jianlong (960), he was made acting Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜左領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed General of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was made General of the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，與其弟審肇、審進皆召赴闕。

translations.literal: In the third year he and his younger brothers Shen Zhao and Shen Jin were all summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he and his brothers Shen Zhao and Shen Jin were summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 審瓊改左龍武軍大將軍，遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Shen Qiong was changed to Grand General of the Left Dragon Martial Army and promoted to Grand General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qiong became Grand General of the Left Dragon Martial Army, then Grand General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，領富州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he held Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande (963) he was made prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官權判右金吾街仗事。

translations.literal: In the third year, with his existing rank he was made acting overseer of the Right Golden Crow Street guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, retaining his rank, he was made acting overseer of the Right Golden Crow Street guard.

sentences.zh: 四年春，步軍帥王繼勳坐事，詔審瓊兼點檢侍衛步軍司事。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year the infantry commander Wang Jixun was implicated in a case; the emperor ordered Shen Qiong also to inspect the Palace Attendant Infantry Command.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4, infantry commander Wang Jixun was implicated in misconduct; Shen Qiong was ordered concurrently to inspect the Palace Attendant Infantry Command.

sentences.zh: 是秋，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: That autumn he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 太祖為廢朝三日，發哀成服，贈太保、寧國軍節度使，諡恭僖。

translations.literal: Taizu suspended court for three days, wore mourning, and posthumously awarded him Grand Tutor and military commissioner of Ningguo Army, with the posthumous name Gongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu suspended court for three days, wore mourning, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor and military commissioner of Ningguo Army, posthumous name Gongxi.

sentences.zh: 審瓊性醇質，在公畏慎，宿衛勤謹，徼巡京邑，里閈清肅，人皆稱之。

translations.literal: Shen Qiong was sincere and plain by nature; in office he was cautious, diligent in palace guard duty, and when patrolling the capital the wards were orderly and all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qiong was sincere and plain; in office he was cautious, diligent in palace guard duty, and when patrolling the capital the neighborhoods were orderly—people praised him.

sentences.zh: 景德三年春，加贈審瓊太傅，妻吳氏陳留郡太夫人。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Jingde, Shen Qiong was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his wife Lady Wu was made Lady of Chenliu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Jingde 3 (1006), Shen Qiong was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his wife Lady Wu was made Lady of Chenliu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是秋，改葬陪陵，又贈審瓊太師、中書令。

translations.literal: That autumn he was reburied beside the imperial tombs; Shen Qiong was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was reburied beside the imperial tombs; Shen Qiong was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子彥圭。

translations.literal: His son was Yan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yan Gui.

sentences.zh: 審肇，建隆三年，起家授左武衛上將軍、檢校左僕射致仕，賜第於京師。

translations.literal: Shen Zhao, in the third year of Jianlong, entered service as General of the Left Martial Guard and acting Left Vice Director, retired, and was granted a mansion in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhao: in Jianlong 3 he entered service as General of the Left Martial Guard and acting Left Vice Director, retired, and was granted a mansion in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，領濰州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he held Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was made prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，改左衛上將軍，仍致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was changed to General of the Left Guard and remained in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 (969) he was made General of the Left Guard and remained retired.

sentences.zh: 三年，起為右驍衛上將軍，俄出知澶州，太祖以審肇未嘗曆郡務，乃命司封郎中姚恕通判州事，以左右之。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled as General of the Right Valiant Cavalry; soon he went out as prefect of Chan. Taizu, because Shen Zhao had never held prefectural duties, ordered Langzhong of the Ministry of Rites Yao Shu to serve as co-administrator to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was recalled as General of the Right Valiant Cavalry; soon he went out as prefect of Chan. Taizu, knowing Shen Zhao had never governed a prefecture, sent Yao Shu of the Ministry of Rites as co-administrator to assist him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，河大決，東彙於鄆、濮數郡，民田罹水害。

translations.literal: Before long the Yellow River burst its banks and waters gathered east in several prefectures of Yan and Pu; civilian fields suffered flood damage.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Yellow River burst its banks; waters pooled east across Yan and Pu prefectures and farmland was flooded.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒其不即時上言，遣使案鞫，遂論恕棄市，審肇免官歸私第。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry that they had not reported promptly; he sent envoys to investigate and Yao Shu was sentenced to execution in the market; Shen Zhao was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was angry they had not reported promptly; he sent investigators; Yao Shu was executed; Shen Zhao was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 俄復舊官，令致仕，特以濰州刺史月奉優給之。

translations.literal: Soon his former office was restored and he was ordered to retire, with his monthly salary as prefect of Wei specially paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his rank was restored and he was ordered to retire, with his Wei prefect monthly salary paid in full.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 太祖廢朝二日，素服發哀，贈太保、昭信軍節度，諡溫肅，遣中使護喪事。

translations.literal: Taizu suspended court two days, wore plain dress and mourned, posthumously awarded him Grand Tutor and military commissioner of Zhaoxin Army, posthumous name Wensu, and sent a palace envoy to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu suspended court two days, wore mourning, posthumously made him Grand Tutor and military commissioner of Zhaoxin Army, posthumous name Wensu, and sent a palace envoy to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，加贈太傅，妻劉氏東海郡太夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his wife Lady Liu was made Lady of Donghai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 he was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his wife Lady Liu was made Lady of Donghai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子彥遵，至南作坊使。

translations.literal: His son Yan Zun rose to commissioner of the Southern workshops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan Zun rose to commissioner of the Southern workshops.

sentences.zh: 審進，建隆三年，起家授右神武大將軍，改右羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: Shen Jin, in the third year of Jianlong, entered service as Grand General of the Right Divine Martial Army and was changed to Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin: in Jianlong 3 he entered service as Grand General of the Right Divine Martial Army, then Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，領賀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande he held He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 1 he was made prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 二年，知陝州。

translations.literal: In the second year he governed Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he governed Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，就改保義軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: In the third year he was at once made military commissioner and observation commissioner of Baoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made military commissioner and observation commissioner of Baoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，加本軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given full military commission of that army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he received full military commission of that army.

sentences.zh: 太祖郊祀西洛，審進來朝，頒賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When Taizu performed suburban sacrifice at the Western Capital, Shen Jin came to court and received very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu performed suburban sacrifice at Luoyang, Shen Jin came to court and received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded, he was made acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, he was made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，會許昌裔刺虢州，捃拾使州闕失事上訴，詔右拾遺李幹鞫之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, when Xu Changyi was prefect of Guo and gathered and reported the prefecture's omissions and faults, the emperor ordered Right Remonstrator Li Gan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 (977), when Xu Changyi was prefect of Guo and reported the prefecture's failures, the emperor ordered Right Remonstrator Li Gan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 幹因上言，請支郡不復隸藩鎮，皆得專達，從之。

translations.literal: Gan memorialized asking that branch prefectures no longer be subordinate to military commissions but report directly; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gan memorialized that branch prefectures should no longer be subordinate to military commissions but report directly; this was approved.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，以審進妻卒，廢朝。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year, because Shen Jin's wife died, court was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 3, because Shen Jin's wife died, court was suspended.

sentences.zh: 十一月郊禮畢，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the suburban rites ended in the eleventh month, he was made acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban rites ended in the eleventh month, he was made acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 四年，上親征河東，審進與嵐州團練使周承晉、德州刺史孫方進、成州刺史慕容福起皆上言願率所部擊太原。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor personally campaigned east against Hedong; Shen Jin with regimental commanders Zhou Chengjin of Lan, Sun Fangjin prefect of De, and Murong Fuqi prefect of Cheng all memorialized wishing to lead their troops to strike Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the emperor campaigned east against Hedong; Shen Jin with Zhou Chengjin of Lan, Sun Fangjin of De, and Murong Fuqi of Cheng all asked to lead their troops against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 上以審進耆年，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shen Jin was advanced in years, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering Shen Jin's age, refused.

sentences.zh: 五年，來朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he came to court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹寇邊，出師捍禦。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan raided the border and troops were sent to defend.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan raided the border and troops marched to defend.

sentences.zh: 上幸大名勞軍，留審進警巡，都邑肅然。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Daming to encourage the army and left Shen Jin to patrol; the capital was solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Daming to encourage the troops and left Shen Jin to patrol; the capital was calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 六年，復歸陝，親王宴餞，供帳甚盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned to Shan; princes gave a farewell feast with lavish provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he returned to Shan; princes gave a lavish farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 其年，就加檢校太師。

translations.literal: That year he was at once made acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was at once made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，上以審進年高，不當煩以劇務，授右衛上將軍，奉給如故。

translations.literal: In summer of the ninth year the emperor, because Shen Jin was old and should not be troubled with heavy duties, appointed him General of the Right Guard with salary unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 9 the emperor, finding Shen Jin too old for heavy duties, made him General of the Right Guard with salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，復授靜江軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was again made military commissioner of Jingjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 (987) he was again made military commissioner of Jingjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，上親耕籍田，審進預其禮，恩賜彌渥，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong the emperor personally plowed the sacred field; Shen Jin took part in the rites, received still richer favor, and was made Commissioner with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1 (988) the emperor plowed the sacred field; Shen Jin took part, received still richer favor, and was made Commissioner with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 上趣駕臨喪，哭之慟，廢朝三日，設次成服，親王公主以下並詣其第舉哀。

translations.literal: The emperor hurried to the mourning hall, wept bitterly, suspended court three days, set up a mourning tent and wore mourning; princes, princesses, and below all went to his residence to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurried to the mourning hall, wept bitterly, suspended court three days, set up mourning, and wore sackcloth; princes, princesses, and all below went to his house to mourn.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，諡恭惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, posthumous name Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, posthumous name Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 審進鎮陝二十餘年，勸農敦本，民庶便之。

translations.literal: Shen Jin governed Shan for more than twenty years, encouraging agriculture and honoring the fundamentals; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin governed Shan for over twenty years, encouraging farming and honoring fundamentals; the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 雖居位節制，無驕矜之色，人推其醇厚。

translations.literal: Though he held a military commission he showed no arrogance; people praised his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held a military commission he showed no arrogance; people praised his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，追封京兆郡王，妻趙氏南陽郡太夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Jingzhao Commandery; his wife Lady Zhao was made Lady of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Jingzhao Commandery; his wife Lady Zhao was made Lady of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後贈尚書令。

translations.literal: Later he was further posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子彥鈞、彥彬。

translations.literal: His sons were Yan Jun and Yan Bin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yan Jun and Yan Bin.

sentences.zh: 彥彬至禮賓副使而卒。

translations.literal: Yan Bin rose to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Ceremonial Guests and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bin rose to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Ceremonial Guests and died.

sentences.zh: 彥圭，起家六宅副使，遷翰林使。

translations.literal: Yan Gui entered service as Vice Commissioner of the Six Residences, and was promoted to Hanlin Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gui entered service as Vice Commissioner of the Six Residences and was promoted Hanlin Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，領信州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he held Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 5 (972) he held Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，改領饒州團練使，俄加領本州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to regimental commander of Rao and soon also given defense of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made regimental commander of Rao and soon also defender of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，與曹翰、孫繼業攻城西面。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan he with Cao Han and Sun Jiye attacked the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he with Cao Han and Sun Jiye attacked the western wall.

sentences.zh: 北征班師，命彥圭與孟玄喆、藥可瓊、趙延進率兵屯中山，坐市竹木矯製免算，責授洛苑使、饒州刺史，裁數日，牽復。

translations.literal: When the northern expedition returned, Yan Gui was ordered with Meng Xuanzhe, Yao Keqiong, and Zhao Yanjin to lead troops stationed at Zhongshan; for falsely reporting bamboo and timber to evade tax he was demoted to Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Rao; within days he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern expedition returned, Yan Gui with Meng Xuanzhe, Yao Keqiong, and Zhao Yanjin were stationed at Zhongshan; for falsely reporting bamboo and timber to evade tax he was demoted to Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Rao; within days he was restored.

sentences.zh: 餘年，遷沙州觀察使，出知定州。

translations.literal: Some years later he was promoted observation commissioner of Sha and went out as prefect of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was made observation commissioner of Sha and went out as prefect of Ding.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中北伐，命副米信為幽州西北道行營都部署。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi northern campaign he was ordered as deputy to Mi Xin, supreme commander of the northwest route army camp for Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi northern campaign he was deputy to Mi Xin, supreme commander of the Youzhou northwest route army.

sentences.zh: 彥圭不容軍士晡食，設陣不整，以致亡失，坐左遷均州團練副使。

translations.literal: Yan Gui would not allow the soldiers their afternoon meal and his battle array was not orderly, causing losses; he was demoted to vice regimental commander of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gui denied soldiers their afternoon meal and his formation was disorderly, causing losses; he was demoted to vice regimental commander of Jun.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，卒於貶所，年五十九，贈歸義軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died at his place of exile, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Guiyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 (985) he died in exile, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Guiyi Army.

sentences.zh: 景德三年春，加贈中書令。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Jingde he was further posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Jingde 3 he was further posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是秋，又贈太師。

translations.literal: That autumn he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子守元。

translations.literal: His son was Shou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 彥鈞，起家補供奉官，累遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: Yan Jun entered service as attendant officer and was promoted repeatedly to Commissioner of Ceremonial Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun entered service as attendant officer and rose to Commissioner of Ceremonial Protocol.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加莊宅使，領羅州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was made Commissioner of the Manor Estates and held Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duangong he was made Commissioner of the Manor Estates and held Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，特置昭宣使，以彥鈞洎王延德、王繼恩為之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua the office of Zhaoxuan Commissioner was specially created; Yan Jun together with Wang Yande and Wang Jien were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4 (993) the office of Zhaoxuan Commissioner was created; Yan Jun with Wang Yande and Wang Jien were appointed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加領恩州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was also given defense of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also given defense of En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 西鄙用兵，命為永興軍駐泊鈐轄。

translations.literal: When war was waged on the western border he was ordered stationed commander at Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out on the western border he was made stationed commander at Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，改領潁州防禦使，出知河中府，占謝便坐，求解內使之職，可之。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded he was changed to defense of Ying, went out as prefect of Hedong, thanked the emperor at an informal audience, and asked to be relieved of inner-palace commissioner duties; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded he was made defender of Ying, went out as prefect of Hedong, thanked the emperor informally, and asked to leave inner-palace office; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 曆知邠、慶、延、鳳四州。

translations.literal: He successively governed Bin, Qing, Yan, and Feng—four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He successively governed Bin, Qing, Yan, and Feng.

sentences.zh: 景德中，為天雄軍副都部署。

translations.literal: In the Jingde period he was deputy supreme commander of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde period he was deputy supreme commander of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 車駕駐澶淵，為駕前東面貝冀路副都部署。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was stationed at Chanyuan, he was deputy supreme commander on the eastern Bei-Ji route before the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Chanyuan, he served as deputy supreme commander on the eastern Bei-Ji route before the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 契丹騎兵攻月城，彥鈞率兵擊走之，以勞優加封邑。

translations.literal: Khitan cavalry attacked the moon city; Yan Jun led troops and drove them off; for his merit his fief was specially increased.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan cavalry attacked the moon city; Yan Jun led troops and drove them off, and his fief was increased for his service.

sentences.zh: 召還，再任河中。

translations.literal: He was recalled and again appointed at Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was again appointed at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 守元，開寶中，補左班殿直，得侍便殿，帶禦器械，遷供奉官、莫州監軍。

translations.literal: Shou Yuan, in the Kaibao period, was appointed Left Class Palace Attendant, attended in the informal hall, carried imperial arms, and was promoted attendant officer and military supervisor of Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Yuan: in the Kaibao period he was made Left Class Palace Attendant, attended in the informal hall, carried imperial arms, and was promoted attendant officer and military supervisor of Mo.

sentences.zh: 契丹入邊，與州將固守城壁，出兵邀擊，獲生口羊馬，以功加崇儀副使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the border he with the prefect held the walls firm, sallied to intercept, captured prisoners and sheep and horses, and for merit was promoted Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border he and the prefect held the walls, sallied to intercept, captured prisoners and livestock, and was promoted Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Protocol.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改正使秩。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to full commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to full commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 曆如京、洛苑使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Commissioner of the Capital and Luoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Commissioner of the Capital and Luoyuan.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，領梧州刺史，連為並代、鎮定、高陽關鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he held Wu Prefecture and was successively stationed commander at Bing-Dai, Zhending, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 3 (997) he held Wu Prefecture and was successively stationed commander at Bing-Dai, Zhending, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，副趙稹使契丹，復涖鎮定。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was deputy to Zhao Zhen on an embassy to the Khitan and again governed Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 2 (1009) he was deputy to Zhao Zhen on an embassy to the Khitan and again governed Zhending.

sentences.zh: 頃之屬疾，詔遣其子殿直惟慶挾太醫乘驛診候，既至而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; the emperor ordered his son Palace Attendant Wei Qing to bring imperial physicians by post horse to examine him; when they arrived he had already died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill; the emperor sent his son Palace Attendant Wei Qing with imperial physicians by courier to examine him; they arrived after he had died, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 惟序字舜功，自三班奉職累遷知惠州、莫州，以供備庫使為梓夔路鈐轄，徙環慶路，知邠州，又權慶州。

translations.literal: Wei Xu, style name Shungong, from Third Class Attendant rose repeatedly to govern Huizhou and Mo; as Supply Commissioner he was stationed commander on Zi-Qi route, moved to Huan-Qing route, governed Bin, and also acted for Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xu, style Shungong, rose from Third Class Attendant to govern Huizhou and Mo; as Supply Commissioner he was stationed commander on the Zi-Qi route, moved to Huan-Qing, governed Bin, and also acted for Qing.

sentences.zh: 會任福敗，以騎兵數千由懷安路破賊三砦，斬首數百級，獲牛馬千計。

translations.literal: When Ren Fu was defeated he with several thousand cavalry by the Huai'an route broke three enemy stockades, beheaded several hundred, and captured over a thousand cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Fu was defeated he led several thousand cavalry by the Huai'an route, broke three enemy stockades, beheaded hundreds, and captured over a thousand cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 以功領忠州刺史，為涇原鈐轄，敕巡警邊州。

translations.literal: For merit he held Zhong Prefecture and was stationed commander of Jingyuan, ordered to patrol the border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he held Zhong Prefecture and was stationed commander of Jingyuan, ordered to patrol border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 久之，改六宅使、知雄州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was changed to Commissioner of the Six Residences and governed Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was made Commissioner of the Six Residences and governed Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時契丹勒兵燕、薊間，遣使求割地。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan massed troops between Yan and Ji and sent envoys seeking ceded territory.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan massed troops between Yan and Ji and sent envoys seeking ceded territory.

sentences.zh: 未至，而惟序購得其草，先以聞。

translations.literal: Before they arrived Wei Xu purchased their draft and reported it first.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived Wei Xu bought their draft and reported it first.

sentences.zh: 徙知滄州，又徙定州。

translations.literal: He was moved to govern Cang and again to Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to govern Cang, then again Ding.

sentences.zh: 再遷東上閣門使、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was again promoted Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and governed Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and governed Jing.

sentences.zh: 改四方館使、知瀛州，復知滄州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Four Directions Hall Commissioner and governed Ying, then again governed Cang.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Four Directions Hall Commissioner and governed Ying, then again Cang.

sentences.zh: 入朝，為祁州團練使，出知恩州，徙大名府路總管，改乾州團練使，卒。

translations.literal: He entered court, was made regimental commander of Qi, went out as prefect of En, was moved to supreme commander of Damingfu route, changed to regimental commander of Qian, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as regimental commander of Qi, went out as prefect of En, was moved to supreme commander of Damingfu route, made regimental commander of Qian, and died.

sentences.zh: 賀令圖，開封陳留人。

translations.literal: Heling Tu, a native of Chenliu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Heling Tu was from Chenliu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父懷浦，孝惠皇后兄也，仕軍中為散指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Huai Pu was the elder brother of Empress Xiaohui and served in the army as commander of the scattered guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huai Pu was Empress Xiaohui's elder brother and served as commander of the scattered guard.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，出為岳州刺史，領兵屯三交。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he went out as prefect of Yue and led troops stationed at Sanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiping Xingguo he went out as prefect of Yue and led troops at Sanjiao.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，從楊業北征，死於陣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he followed Yang Ye on the northern expedition and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3 (986) he followed Yang Ye on the northern expedition and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 令圖少謹願，隸太宗左右，洎即位，補供奉官，改綾錦副使、知莫州，遷崇儀使、知雄州。

translations.literal: Ling Tu was cautious and compliant from youth and served Taizong's side; when Taizong succeeded he was made attendant officer, changed to deputy commissioner of brocade and prefect of Mo, and promoted Ceremonial Protocol Commissioner and prefect of Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu was cautious from youth and served at Taizong's side; when Taizong succeeded he was made attendant officer, then deputy brocade commissioner and prefect of Mo, then Ceremonial Protocol Commissioner and prefect of Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，領平州刺史，充幽州行營壕砦使，以所部下固安、新城兩縣，克涿州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he held Ping Prefecture as trench and stockade commissioner of the Youzhou field army; with his subordinates he took the two counties of Gu'an and Xincheng and captured Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he held Ping Prefecture as trench commissioner of the Youzhou field army; with his troops he took Gu'an and Xincheng counties and captured Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會父戰死，起家為六宅使，領本州團練使，護瀛州屯兵。

translations.literal: When his father died in battle he entered service as Commissioner of the Six Residences and regimental commander of that prefecture, protecting Ying border troops.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died in battle he entered service as Commissioner of the Six Residences and regimental commander of that prefecture, protecting Ying border troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，令圖握兵邊郡十餘年，恃藩邸舊恩，每歲入奏事，多言邊塞利害，及幽薊可取之狀。

translations.literal: Earlier Ling Tu had held border troops for more than ten years; relying on old favor from the princely residence, each year when he reported he often spoke of border advantages and disadvantages and how You-Ji could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ling Tu had held border command for over ten years; relying on old favor from Taizong's princely days, each year at court he spoke of border conditions and how You and Ji could be taken.

sentences.zh: 上信之，故有岐溝之舉。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted him, and therefore there was the Qigou campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him, and therefore launched the Qigou campaign.

sentences.zh: 既而師敗，議者皆咎其貪功生事。

translations.literal: After the army was defeated critics all blamed his greed for merit and provoking trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat critics blamed his greed for glory and provoking war.

sentences.zh: 令圖輕而無謀，契丹將耶律遜寧號於越者，使諜紿令圖曰：「我獲罪本國，旦夕願歸南朝，無路自拔，幸君侯少留意焉。」

translations.literal: Ling Tu was rash and without counsel; the Khitan general Yelü Xunnin, titled Yuyue, had a spy deceive Ling Tu saying: 'I have offended my state and wish daily to return to the Southern Court but have no way to escape; I hope you will take a little notice.'
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu was rash and unwise; the Khitan general Yelü Xunnin, titled Yuyue, sent a spy who told Ling Tu: 'I have offended my country and wish daily to defect to the Song but cannot; I hope you will take notice.'

sentences.zh: 令圖不虞其詐，私遺以重錦十兩。

translations.literal: Ling Tu did not suspect the deception and privately sent him ten liang of heavy brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu did not suspect fraud and privately sent him ten liang of heavy brocade.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，於越率眾入寇，大將劉廷讓與戰於君子館，令圖為先鋒，被圍數重。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year Yuyue led a host to raid; Grand General Liu Tingrang fought him at Junzi Lodge; Ling Tu was vanguard and was surrounded many times.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month Yuyue led troops to raid; Liu Tingrang fought at Junzi Lodge; Ling Tu was vanguard and was surrounded many times.

sentences.zh: 於越傳言軍中「願得見雄州賀使君。」

translations.literal: Yuyue spread word in the army: 'I wish to see Commissioner Heling of Xiong Prefecture.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuyue spread word in the army: 'I wish to see Commissioner Heling of Xiong Prefecture.'

sentences.zh: 令圖嘗為所紿，意其來降而終獲大功，即引麾下數十騎逆之。

translations.literal: Ling Tu had once been deceived by him and thought he came to surrender and would at last win great merit; he led several dozen horsemen to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu, having been deceived before, thought Yuyue came to surrender and he would win great merit; he led several dozen horsemen to meet him.

sentences.zh: 將至其帳數步外，於越據床罵曰：「汝常好經度邊事，乃今送死來邪！」

translations.literal: When he was several paces from the tent Yuyue sat on the bed and cursed: 'You always loved to plan border affairs—now you have come to die!'
translations.idiomatic: When he was several paces from the tent Yuyue sat on the bed and cursed: 'You always loved to plan border affairs—now you have come to die!'

sentences.zh: 麾左右盡殺其從騎，反縛令圖而去。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to kill all his escort horsemen and bound Ling Tu and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to kill all Ling Tu's escort and bound Ling Tu and took him away.

sentences.zh: 令圖與其父首謀北伐，一歲中父子皆陷焉。

translations.literal: Ling Tu with his father had chiefly urged the northern expedition; within one year father and son both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu and his father had chiefly urged the northern expedition; within one year father and son both fell.

sentences.zh: 令圖時年三十九。

translations.literal: Ling Tu was then thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tu was then thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 是役也，武州防禦使、高陽關部署楊重進死之。

translations.literal: In this campaign Military Supervisor Yang Chongjin of Gaoyang Pass also died.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Yang Chongjin, military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass, also died.

sentences.zh: 重進，太原人。

translations.literal: Chongjin was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少有膂力，周祖鎮大名，以隸帳下，廣順初，補衛士。

translations.literal: From youth he had strength; when Zhou Taizu held Daming he was placed in the entourage; at the beginning of Guangshun he was made a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was strong; when Zhou Taizu held Daming he joined his entourage; at Guangshun's start he became a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 宋初，累遷至內殿直都虞候。

translations.literal: In early Song he was promoted repeatedly to Vice Commander of the Inner Hall Direct.
translations.idiomatic: In early Song he rose to Vice Commander of the Inner Hall Direct.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，改龍衛軍都校，領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was changed to Colonel of the Dragon Guard and held Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiping Xingguo's start he was made Colonel of the Dragon Guard and held Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，出為萊州刺史。

translations.literal: On the Taiyuan campaign he went out as prefect of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he went out as prefect of Lai.

sentences.zh: 隨曹彬北征，為右廂排陣使，改武州防禦使、高陽關部署。

translations.literal: Following Cao Bin on the northern expedition he was right-wing array commander, changed to defense of Wu and military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Following Cao Bin north he was right-wing array commander, then defender of Wu and military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 會契丹兵至，與之力戰，遂沒於陣。

translations.literal: When Khitan troops arrived he fought them fiercely and perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan troops arrived he fought fiercely and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 年六十五。

translations.literal: He was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 王繼勳，彰德節度饒之子，孝明皇后同母弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Jixun was son of the military commissioner of Raode; he was younger brother by the same mother of Empress Xiaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixun was son of the Raode military commissioner and Empress Xiaoming's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 生時，其母見一人赤髮，狀貌怪異，入室中，遂生繼勳。

translations.literal: At his birth his mother saw a man with red hair and strange appearance enter the room, and then Jixun was born.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth his mother saw a red-haired man of strange appearance enter the room, and Jixun was born.

sentences.zh: 及長，美風儀，性凶率無賴。

translations.literal: When grown he had fine bearing but a fierce, reckless nature.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he had fine bearing but was fierce and reckless.

sentences.zh: 以後故，為內殿供奉官、都知、溪州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of the empress he was made inner-hall attendant officer, director, and prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Through the empress he was made inner-hall attendant, director, and prefect of Xi.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，加領恩州團練使，又改龍捷右廂都指揮使，尋領永州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was also given regimental command of En and changed to commander of the right Dragon Swift wing; soon he held defense of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was also given regimental command of En and made commander of the right Dragon Swift wing; soon defender of Yong.

sentences.zh: 四年，收復湖南，改領彭州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Hunan was recovered and he was changed to defense of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Hunan was recovered and he was made defender of Peng.

sentences.zh: 是秋，將討西蜀，命繼勳戒期，將大閱。

translations.literal: That autumn when Western Shu was to be attacked Jixun was ordered to keep the deadline and a great review was held.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, preparing to attack Shu, Jixun was ordered to keep the deadline and a great review was held.

sentences.zh: 繼勳素與大校馬仁瑀不協，陰勒部下市白梃，將以相圖。

translations.literal: Jixun had long been at odds with senior commander Ma Renyu and secretly urged his men to buy white clubs intending to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun had long feuded with Ma Renyu and secretly had his men buy white clubs to fight him.

sentences.zh: 太祖知之，為出仁瑀密州。

translations.literal: Taizu learned of it and sent Renyu out to Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu learned of it and sent Renyu to Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄遷保寧軍節度觀察留後、領虎捷左右廂都虞候、權侍衛步軍司事。

translations.literal: Soon Jixun was moved to observation commissioner of Baoning and commander of both Tiger Swift wings and acting overseer of the Palace Attendant Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jixun was made observation commissioner of Baoning, commander of both Tiger Swift wings, and acting overseer of Palace Attendant Infantry.

sentences.zh: 繼勳所為多不法。

translations.literal: Jixun's conduct was often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun often acted unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 會新募兵千餘隸雄武，將遣出征，多無妻室，太祖謂繼勳曰：「此必有願為婚者，不須備聘財，但酒炙可也。」

translations.literal: When over a thousand newly recruited troops of the Valiant Martial were to be sent on campaign, most had no wives; Taizu told Jixun: 'Among these there must be some wishing to marry; no betrothal gifts need be prepared—only wine and meat will do.'
translations.idiomatic: When over a thousand new Valiant Martial recruits were to march, most had no wives; Taizu told Jixun: 'Some must wish to marry; no betrothal gifts—wine and meat will suffice.'

sentences.zh: 繼勳不能諭上旨，縱令掠人子女，京城為之紛擾。

translations.literal: Jixun could not grasp the emperor's intent and allowed his men to seize people's sons and daughters; the capital was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun missed the emperor's meaning and let his men seize people's children; the capital was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 上聞大驚，遣捕斬百餘人，人情始定。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly alarmed and sent men to capture and execute over a hundred; public feeling then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and had over a hundred captured and executed; order returned.

sentences.zh: 時後已崩，上追念後，故不之罪也。

translations.literal: The empress had already died; the emperor recalled the empress and therefore did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had already died; remembering her, the emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，繼勳復為部曲所訟，詔中書鞫之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande Jixun was again sued by his troops; the emperor ordered the Secretariat to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 4 his troops sued him again; the Secretariat was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 解兵柄，為彰國軍留後，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His military power was removed; he was made military commissioner of Zhangguo and attended court.
translations.idiomatic: His command was removed; he was made Zhangguo military commissioner and attended court.

sentences.zh: 繼勳自以失職，常怏怏，專以臠割奴婢為樂，前後多被害。

translations.literal: Jixun felt himself displaced and was always resentful, taking pleasure in cutting up slave girls and boys; many were harmed before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun, feeling displaced, was resentful and amused himself by cutting up slave girls and boys; many died.

sentences.zh: 一日，天雨牆壞，群婢突出，守國門訴冤。

translations.literal: One day rain broke the wall and slave girls burst out and appealed for justice at the National Gate.
translations.idiomatic: One day rain broke a wall and slave girls burst out and appealed at the National Gate.

sentences.zh: 上大駭，命中使就詰之，盡得繼勳所為不法事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed and ordered a palace envoy to question him; all Jixun's unlawful acts were fully obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and sent a palace envoy to question him; all his crimes were exposed.

sentences.zh: 詔削奪官爵，勒歸私第，仍令甲士守之。

translations.literal: He was ordered stripped of rank and enfeoffment and sent to his private residence with armored soldiers to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank and sent home under armed guard.

sentences.zh: 俄又配流登州，未至，改右監門率府副率。

translations.literal: Soon he was exiled to Dengzhou; before arriving he was changed to Vice Director of the Right Prison Gate Rate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was exiled to Dengzhou; before arrival he was made Vice Director of the Right Prison Gate Rate.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，命分司西京。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was ordered to serve at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3 he was ordered to serve at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 繼勳殘暴愈甚，強市民家子女備給使，小不如意，即殺食之，而棺其骨棄野外。

translations.literal: Jixun grew still more brutal, forcibly buying commoners' sons and daughters for servants; at the slightest displeasure he killed and ate them and threw the bones in coffins in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun grew more brutal, forcibly buying people's children as servants; at slight displeasure he killed and ate them and threw bones in coffins outdoors.

sentences.zh: 女儈及鬻棺者出入其門不絕，洛民苦之而不敢告。

translations.literal: Female brokers and coffin sellers passed his gate without cease; Luoyang people suffered but dared not report.
translations.idiomatic: Brokers and coffin sellers never left his gate; Luoyang people suffered but dared not report.

sentences.zh: 太宗在藩邸，頗聞其事。

translations.literal: Taizong in the princely residence had often heard of these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong at the princely residence had often heard of this.

sentences.zh: 及即位，人有訴者，命戶部員外郎、知雜事雷德驤乘傳往鞫之。

translations.literal: When he succeeded someone complained; he ordered Ministry of Revenue Outer Section Officer Lei Dezao to go by post horse to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded, someone complained; he sent Lei Dezao of the Revenue Ministry by courier to investigate.

sentences.zh: 繼勳具伏，自開寶六年四月至太平興國二年二月，手所殺婢百餘人。

translations.literal: Jixun fully confessed; from the fourth month of Kaibao 6 to the second month of Taiping Xingguo 2 he had personally killed over a hundred slave girls.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun confessed fully: from Kaibao 6 month 4 to Taiping Xingguo 2 month 2 he had personally killed over a hundred slave girls.

sentences.zh: 乃斬繼勳洛陽市，及為強市子女者女儈八人、男子三人。

translations.literal: Jixun was executed in Luoyang market together with eight female brokers and three men who had forcibly bought children for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was executed in Luoyang market with eight brokers and three men who had supplied children.

sentences.zh: 長壽寺僧廣惠常與繼勳同食人肉，令折其脛而斬之。

translations.literal: Changsou Temple monk Guanghui had often eaten human flesh with Jixun; he was ordered to have his shins broken and then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Monk Guanghui of Changshou Temple had often eaten human flesh with Jixun; his shins were broken and he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 洛民稱快。

translations.literal: Luoyang people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 其後家寓西洛潁陽，孫惟德不肖，不能自立，丐食以給。

translations.literal: Later his family lived in Yingyang west of Luoyang; grandson Weide was worthless and could not support himself and begged for food.
translations.idiomatic: Later his family lived west of Luoyang at Yingyang; grandson Weide was worthless and begged for food.

sentences.zh: 真宗聞而憫之，授惟德汝州司士參軍。

translations.literal: Zhenzong heard and pitied him and appointed Weide Assistant Magistrate of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong pitied him and made Weide Assistant Magistrate of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉知信字至誠，邢州人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhixin, style name Zhicheng, was a native of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixin, style Zhicheng, was from Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父遷，晉天福末鳳翔帳前軍使，改滑州奉國軍校，從驍將皇甫暉禦邊有功，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Qian served in the Later Jin as commander of the Fengxiang front army, changed to Fengguo Army school at Hua, followed the fierce general Huangfu Hui on the border with merit, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian served the Later Jin as Fengxiang front-army commander, then Fengguo Army school at Hua, followed Huangfu Hui on the border with merit, and died young.

sentences.zh: 母即昭憲太后之妹也，乾德初，封京兆郡太君，六年，進本郡太夫人，開寶三年十月卒。

translations.literal: His mother was younger sister of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian; at the beginning of Qiande she was enfeoffed Lady of Jingzhao Commandery; in the sixth year she was advanced to Grand Lady of that commandery; in the tenth month of Kaibao 3 she died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Dowager Zhaoxian's younger sister; in Qiande's start she was made Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, advanced in year 6 to Grand Lady, and died Kaibao 3 month 10.

sentences.zh: 太祖廢朝發哀，追封齊國太夫人，陪葬安陵，贈遷太保。

translations.literal: Taizu suspended court and mourned, posthumously enfeoffed her Grand Lady of Qi, buried beside Anling, and posthumously made Qian Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu suspended court, mourned, posthumously made her Grand Lady of Qi, buried her beside Anling, and posthumously made Qian Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 知信三歲而孤，宣祖憐其敏慧。

translations.literal: Zhixin was orphaned at three; Emperor Xuan pitied his cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin was orphaned at three; Emperor Xuan pitied his cleverness.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，起家授供奉官，丁內艱，轉六宅副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he entered service as attendant officer; on inner mourning he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 3 he entered service as attendant officer; on mourning for his mother he became Vice Commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，遷軍器庫使，掌武德司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was promoted Arsenal Commissioner and managed the Wude Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 5 he was promoted Arsenal Commissioner and managed the Wude Office.

sentences.zh: 六年，領錦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he held Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he held Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬郊祀西洛，為行宮使，駐洛中，又為西京武德、皇城、宮苑等使。

translations.literal: When suburban sacrifice was at the Western Capital he was traveling-palace commissioner and stationed at Luoyang; he was also commissioner of Western Capital Wude, Imperial City, and Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: When suburban sacrifice was at Luoyang he was traveling-palace commissioner there and also commissioner of Wude, Imperial City, and Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 車駕出郊，又充大內留守。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to the suburbs he also served as inner-palace custodian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to the suburbs he also served as inner-palace custodian.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，改左神武軍將軍，尋領檀州團練使，護屯兵於鎮州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was changed to General of the Left Divine Martial Army; soon he held regimental command of Tan and protected troops at Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxi's start he was made General of the Left Divine Martial Army; soon regimental commander of Tan protecting troops at Zhen.

sentences.zh: 會大舉北伐，與六宅使符昭壽為押陣都監。

translations.literal: When the great northern campaign was launched he with Six Residences Commissioner Fu Zhaoshou were supreme array supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: On the great northern campaign he with Fu Zhaoshou were supreme array supervisors.

sentences.zh: 師還，諸將失道，知信獨整所部以歸。

translations.literal: When the army returned the generals lost their way; only Zhixin brought his command back in order.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the generals lost their way; only Zhixin brought his command back intact.

sentences.zh: 俄知定州兼兵馬鈐轄，押大陣右偏。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Ding and concurrently was military supervisor, commanding the right wing of the great array.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Ding and was military supervisor, commanding the right wing.

sentences.zh: 一日，宴犒將士，契丹騎乘間至，知信不介而出，追之數十里，斬獲甚眾，以功就拜邕州觀察使。

translations.literal: One day feasting and rewarding the troops, Khitan cavalry suddenly arrived; Zhixin went out without armor, pursued them several tens of li, beheaded and captured many, and for merit was at once made observation commissioner of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: One day while feasting his troops Khitan cavalry suddenly arrived; Zhixin went out unarmored, pursued tens of li, killed and captured many, and was made observation commissioner of Yong.

sentences.zh: 四年，召入，改并州路副都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned in and made deputy supreme commander of Bingzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was summoned and made deputy supreme commander of Bingzhou route.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，代還，知杭州。

translations.literal: In the Duangong period he returned on replacement and governed Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong he returned and governed Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，又知天雄軍府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he again governed Tianxiong Army prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4 he again governed Tianxiong Army prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，充修奉永熙陵部署。

translations.literal: When Taizong died he was made commissioner for repairing and serving Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died he was made commissioner for repairing and serving Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，拜建武軍節度觀察留後，知永平軍府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made observation commissioner and military commissioner of Jianwu Army and governed Yongping Army prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianping's start he was made observation commissioner of Jianwu Army and governed Yongping Army prefecture.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，復知天雄軍。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the border he again governed Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border he again governed Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗北巡，充駕前副都部署，曆知河陽、升州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong toured the north he was deputy supreme commander before the imperial presence and successively governed Heyang and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhenzong's northern tour he was deputy supreme commander before the emperor and successively governed Heyang and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，車駕幸澶淵，命為東京都巡檢使，復知定州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde when the imperial carriage was at Chanyuan he was made eastern capital patrol commissioner and again governed Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 1 when the emperor was at Chanyuan he was eastern capital patrol commissioner and again governed Ding.

sentences.zh: 二年，以疾求還京，至鎮州卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the second year he asked to return to the capital on illness; he died at Zhen Prefecture, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he asked to return on illness and died at Zhen Prefecture, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈太尉、天平軍節度。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and military commissioner of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and military commissioner of Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 知信以戚裏致貴，尤被親任，中外踐曆，最為舊故。

translations.literal: Zhixin rose to wealth through consort kin and was especially trusted and employed; inside and outside he held many posts and was the oldest intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin rose through consort kin and was especially trusted; he held many posts inside and outside and was the longest-serving intimate.

sentences.zh: 雖無顯赫稱，亦以循謹聞於時。

translations.literal: Though he had no brilliant reputation he was known in his time for circumspection.
translations.idiomatic: Though without brilliant fame he was known for circumspection.

sentences.zh: 子承宗、承渥。

translations.literal: His sons were Chengzong and Chenwo.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chengzong and Chenwo.

sentences.zh: 承宗，幼善射，兼習書數，以蔭補殿直，寄班祗候。

translations.literal: Chengzong from youth was skilled at archery and also studied writing and calculation; by yin privilege he was made Palace Attendant and attached attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong from youth was skilled at archery and studied writing; by yin privilege he was made Palace Attendant and attached attendant.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，轉供奉官、鎮、定、高陽關三路承受公事，還，掌軍器庫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was changed to attendant officer and receiver of official business on the Zhen-Ding-Gaoyang route; on return he managed the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianping's start he was attendant officer on the Zhen-Ding-Gaoyang route; on return he managed the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 會真宗臨幸，見其整肅，麵授閣門祗候。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited in person and saw his orderliness he was face-to-face appointed Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong visited and saw his orderliness he was appointed Gate Attendant on the spot.

sentences.zh: 知信卒，轉內殿崇班。

translations.literal: When Zhixin died he was changed to Inner Hall Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixin died he was promoted Inner Hall Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為河北緣邊安撫都監。

translations.literal: Before long he was frontier pacification supervisor of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Hebei frontier pacification supervisor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，就加內殿承製，曆如京、文思二副使，徙河東緣邊安撫，又知保州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was at once made Inner Hall Fabricator; he successively served as Vice Commissioner of Capital and Literary Splendor; he was moved to Hedong frontier pacification and also governed Bao.
translations.idiomatic: At Dazhong Xiangfu's start he was Inner Hall Fabricator; he served as Vice Commissioner of Capital and Literary Splendor; moved to Hedong frontier pacification and governed Bao.

sentences.zh: 俄拜東染院使、知定州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Eastern Dyeing Commissioner and governed Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Eastern Dyeing Commissioner and governed Ding.

sentences.zh: 副薛映使契丹，使還，歸本任，又兼鎮定路兵馬鈐轄，俄改宮苑使、知雄州、河北緣邊安撫使。

translations.literal: Deputy to Xue Ying on embassy to Khitan; on return he resumed his post and was also military supervisor of Zhending route; soon he was Palace Parks Commissioner, prefect of Xiong, and Hebei frontier pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy to Xue Ying on embassy to Khitan; on return he resumed office and was military supervisor of Zhending; soon Palace Parks Commissioner, prefect of Xiong, and Hebei frontier pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 在郡有治跡，詔書嘉獎，召歸，時靈昌決河初塞，擇守臣，以承宗為皇城使、知滑州。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he had governing traces; an edict praised him and he was recalled; when the Lingchang Yellow River was first blocked they chose a guardian and made Chengzong Imperial City Commissioner and prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He governed well; an edict praised him and recalled him; when the Lingchang breach was first sealed he was made Imperial City Commissioner and prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復代還。

translations.literal: Before long he returned on replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned on replacement.

sentences.zh: 會西邊言吐蕃唃斯囉作文法，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: When the western border reported that the Tibetan Gusiluo was establishing laws and was quite a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When the western border reported Tibetan Gusiluo was establishing laws and troubling the frontier.

sentences.zh: 命副龍圖閣直學士陳堯谘為鄜延、邠寧環慶、涇原儀渭、秦州路巡撫使，詔令堯谘等所至軍州犒官吏將校，諮訪民間利害、郡官使臣能否功過以聞。

translations.literal: He was ordered deputy to Longtu Pavilion Academician Chen Yaozou as pacification commissioner on the Fuyan, Binning-Huanqing, Jingyuan-Yiwei, and Qin routes; the edict ordered Yaozou and others at each army and prefecture to reward officials and officers and consult on popular benefit and harm and the ability and faults of prefectural officials and envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He was deputy to Chen Yaozou as pacification commissioner on western routes; the edict ordered them to reward officers and inquire into popular welfare and officials' merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 或有陳訴屈抑，經轉運、提點司區斷不當，即按鞫詣實，杖以下依法區理，徒以上驛聞，仍取係囚躬親錄問，催促論決。

translations.literal: Where there were appeals of wrongs not properly judged by transport or investigation offices, they should investigate the facts, punish with staff those below the law, report those above by courier, still take prisoners and personally record and question them, and urge decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Where appeals were wrongly judged by transport or investigation offices they should investigate, punish lesser offenders with staff, report greater ones by courier, examine prisoners personally, and urge decisions.

sentences.zh: 既行，就命堯谘知秦州，承宗為西上閣門使，充鈐轄。

translations.literal: On departure Yaozou was at once made prefect of Qin and Chengzong was Western Upper Gate Commissioner and stationed commander.
translations.idiomatic: On departure Yaozou was made prefect of Qin and Chengzong Western Upper Gate Commissioner and stationed commander.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，進東上閣門使，徒鄜延都鈐轄而卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was promoted Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, moved to Fuyan supreme commander, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianxing's start he was Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, moved to Fuyan supreme commander, and died.

sentences.zh: 中使護柩至京師，賜以葬地。

translations.literal: A palace envoy escorted the coffin to the capital and burial land was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy escorted the coffin to the capital and burial land was granted.

sentences.zh: 承渥蔭補殿直，累任使，喜為條奏，至供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Chenwo by yin privilege was made Palace Attendant, held envoy posts repeatedly, liked to submit memorials on regulations, and rose to attendant officer and Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chenwo by yin privilege was Palace Attendant, held envoy posts, liked regulatory memorials, and rose to attendant officer and Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 承宗子永釗，右侍禁、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Chengzong's son Yongzhao was Right Attendant Forbidden and Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong's son Yongzhao was Right Attendant Forbidden and Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉文裕，字以寧，保州保塞人。

translations.literal: Liu Wenyu, style name Yining, was a native of Baose in Bao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenyu, style Yining, was from Baose in Bao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖正，晉幽州營田使兼平州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zheng was Jin Youzhou agricultural commissioner and concurrent prefect of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zheng was Jin Youzhou agricultural commissioner and concurrent prefect of Ping.

sentences.zh: 父審奇，武牢關使。

translations.literal: His father Shenqi was Wulao Pass commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenqi was Wulao Pass commissioner.

sentences.zh: 簡穆皇后即文裕祖姑也。

translations.literal: Empress Jianmu was Wenyu's grandfather's sister.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jianmu was Wenyu's grandfather's sister.

sentences.zh: 審奇三子，長文遠，建隆中為供奉官，與並人戰萬善而沒。

translations.literal: Shenqi had three sons; the eldest Wenyuan in Jianlong was attendant officer and died fighting the Bing at Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi had three sons; eldest Wenyuan in Jianlong was attendant officer and died fighting Bing at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 次即文裕，開寶四年，起家補殿直。

translations.literal: Next was Wenyu; in the fourth year of Kaibao he entered service as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Wenyu; in Kaibao 4 he entered service as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，權管雲騎員僚直，預討江南，中弩矢，神色自若。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as commander of the Cloud Cavalry attendants and took part in the Jiangnan campaign; hit by a crossbow bolt he remained calm in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he commanded Cloud Cavalry attendants on the Jiangnan campaign; struck by a crossbow bolt he remained calm.

sentences.zh: 太宗在藩邸，多得親接。

translations.literal: Taizong in the princely residence had often received him personally.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong in the princely residence had often received him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，擢為內弓箭庫副使，特封其母張氏清河縣太君，出為秦、隴巡檢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted Vice Commissioner of the Inner Bow and Arrow Arsenal and his mother Lady Zhang was specially enfeoffed Grand Lady of Qinghe County; he went out as inspector of Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he was promoted Vice Commissioner of the Inner Bow and Arrow Arsenal; his mother Lady Zhang was made Grand Lady of Qinghe County; he went out as Qin-Long inspector.

sentences.zh: 有李飛雄者，太保致仕鏻之孫，秦州節度判官若愚之子。

translations.literal: There was one Li Feixiong, grandson of the retired Grand Tutor Lin, son of Qin military commissioner Ruoyu's son.
translations.idiomatic: There was Li Feixiong, grandson of retired Grand Tutor Lin, son of Qin military commissioner Ruoyu.

sentences.zh: 性凶險，不為其家所容，常往來京師、魏博間，與無賴惡少遊處，縱酒蒲博為務。

translations.literal: By nature fierce and dangerous, not tolerated by his family, he often traveled between the capital and Weibo with worthless ruffians, making drinking and gambling his business.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and dangerous, not tolerated at home, he traveled between capital and Weibo with ruffians, drinking and gambling.

sentences.zh: 以其父故，盡知秦州倉庫所積，及地形險易、兵籍多少。

translations.literal: Because of his father he fully knew Qin Prefecture storehouses and terrain and the size of military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father he knew Qin storehouses, terrain, and military registers.

sentences.zh: 又有妻父張季英為鳳翔盩厔尉，飛雄自京師往省之，因乘季英馬詐為使者，夜抵廄置呼卒索馬。

translations.literal: Also his wife's father Zhang Jiying was Fengxiang Zhouzhi county captain; Feixiong went from the capital to visit him and by riding Jiying's horse pretended to be an envoy, reached the stable at night and called for a groom to saddle a horse.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Zhang Jiying was Fengxiang Zhouzhi captain; Feixiong visited him, took his horse, pretended to be an envoy, reached a stable at night and demanded a horse.

sentences.zh: 卒秉炬出迎，飛雄以私市馬纓示之，卒不能辨，即授以馬。

translations.literal: A soldier came out with a torch to welcome him; Feixiong showed a privately bought bridle and the soldier could not tell and gave him the horse.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier came out with a torch; Feixiong showed a private bridle; the soldier could not tell and gave him the horse.

sentences.zh: 一卒乘一馬前導，以巡邊為名，因矯詔率巡驛殿直姚承遂，至隴州率監軍供奉官王守定，至吳山縣率縣尉盧讚，皆從行。

translations.literal: One soldier rode one horse ahead as guide in the name of patrolling the border; thus with forged edict he led patrol post Palace Attendant Yao Chengsui, at Long led military supervisor attendant Wang Shouding, at Wushan led county captain Lu Zan—all followed.
translations.idiomatic: One soldier rode ahead as border patrol guide; with forged edict he led Yao Chengsui at Long, Wang Shouding at Long's military supervisor post, Lu Zan at Wushan—all followed.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦州內屬，羌人為寇，朝廷遣周承晉、田仁朗、王侁、梁崇讚、韋韜、馬知節及文裕領兵屯清水縣，飛雄至，稱製盡縛之。

translations.literal: Earlier Qin had submitted and Qiang raided; the court sent Zhou Chengjin, Tian Renlang, Wang You, Liang Chongzan, Wei Tao, Ma Zhijie, and Wenyu with troops stationed at Qingshui; when Feixiong arrived he claimed an edict to bind them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qin had submitted and Qiang raided; the court sent Zhou Chengjin, Tian Renlang, Wang You, Liang Chongzan, Wei Tao, Ma Zhijie, and Wenyu to Qingshui; Feixiong arrived claiming an edict to bind them all.

sentences.zh: 承晉等見姚承遂數輩同至，不覺其詐。

translations.literal: Chengjin and the others seeing Yao Chengsui and several arrive did not notice the fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjin and others seeing Chengsui arrive did not notice the fraud.

sentences.zh: 仁朗獨號泣求詔書，飛雄叱之曰：「我受密旨，以若輩逗撓不用命，令盡誅。

translations.literal: Only Renlang alone wept and begged for the edict; Feixiong rebuked him: 'I received a secret edict because you delay and disobey orders and ordered all to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Renlang wept and begged for the edict; Feixiong rebuked him: 'I have a secret edict because you delay and disobey— all are to be executed.

sentences.zh: 汝豈不聞封州殺李鶴邪？

translations.literal: Have you not heard that Feng Prefecture killed Li He?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard Feng Prefecture killed Li He?

sentences.zh: 詔書汝豈得見！」

translations.literal: How can you see the edict!
translations.idiomatic: How can you see the edict!

sentences.zh: 先是，上即位，分命親信於諸道廉官吏善惡密以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier when the emperor succeeded he assigned trusted men to each route to secretly report officials' good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when the emperor succeeded he assigned trusted men on each route to secretly report officials' conduct.

sentences.zh: 嶺南使者言封州李鶴不奉法，誣奏軍吏謀反，詔即誅之。

translations.literal: The Lingnan envoy said Feng Prefecture's Li He did not obey law and falsely reported military clerks plotting rebellion; an edict immediately executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingnan envoy said Li He of Feng Prefecture disobeyed law and falsely reported a military plot; an edict had him executed at once.

sentences.zh: 故飛雄引以為言。

translations.literal: Therefore Feixiong cited this as his words.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Feixiong cited this.

sentences.zh: 將械承晉等詣秦州戮之，因據城叛，遂驅承晉等行。

translations.literal: He was about to shackle Chengjin and the others and take them to Qin to execute and rebel by holding the city and drove Chengjin and the others onward.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to shackle Chengjin and others, execute them at Qin, seize the city and rebel, and drove them onward.

sentences.zh: 初，飛雄詐宣製時，自言我上南府時親吏，文裕因哀告飛雄曰：「我亦嘗依晉邸，使者豈不營救之乎？」

translations.literal: When Feixiong falsely proclaimed the edict he said he had been a close clerk when the emperor was at the southern residence; Wenyu therefore pleaded with Feixiong: 'I also once served the Jin residence—will the envoy not rescue me?'
translations.idiomatic: When Feixiong falsely proclaimed the edict he said he had been close clerk at the southern residence; Wenyu pleaded: 'I also served the Jin residence—will you not save me?'

sentences.zh: 飛雄低語謂文裕曰：「 爾能與我同富貴否？」

translations.literal: Feixiong whispered to Wenyu: 'Can you share wealth and honor with me?'
translations.idiomatic: Feixiong whispered: 'Can you share wealth and honor with me?'

sentences.zh: 文裕覺其詐，偽許之。

translations.literal: Wenyu perceived the fraud and falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sensed the fraud and falsely agreed.

sentences.zh: 飛雄即命左右釋文裕縛。

translations.literal: Feixiong then ordered attendants to release Wenyu's bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Feixiong then ordered Wenyu's bonds released.

sentences.zh: 文裕策馬前附耳語仁朗，仁朗佯墜馬，若卒中風眩狀。

translations.literal: Wenyu spurred his horse forward and whispered to Renlang; Renlang pretended to fall from his horse as if stricken by wind.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu spurred forward and whispered to Renlang; Renlang pretended to fall as if stricken.

sentences.zh: 飛雄共前視之，又釋其縛。

translations.literal: Feixiong all went forward to look and again released his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Feixiong all went to look and again released his bonds.

sentences.zh: 仁朗奮起搏飛雄，與文裕共擒之。

translations.literal: Renlang sprang up and grappled Feixiong; with Wenyu they seized him together.
translations.idiomatic: Renlang sprang up and grappled Feixiong; with Wenyu they seized him.

sentences.zh: 飛雄尚呼云：「田仁郎等謀反殺使者。」

translations.literal: Feixiong still cried: 'Tian Renlang and others plot rebellion and kill the envoy.'
translations.idiomatic: Feixiong still cried: 'Tian Renlang and others rebel and kill the envoy!'

sentences.zh: 送秦州獄鞫得實，飛雄、承遂、守定、讚坐要斬，夷飛雄家。

translations.literal: Sent to Qin prison; investigation obtained the truth; Feixiong, Chengsui, Shouding, and Zan were executed by waist-slicing; Feixiong's family was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Qin prison; truth obtained; Feixiong, Chengsui, Shouding, and Zan were waist-sliced; Feixiong's family exterminated.

sentences.zh: 捕先與飛雄善者何大舉等數輩，悉棄市，廄置卒亦夷其族。

translations.literal: Those earlier friendly with Feixiong such as He Daju were captured several and all abandoned in market; stable soldiers were also exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Those friendly with Feixiong such as He Daju were captured and executed; stable soldiers' families were also exterminated.

sentences.zh: 因下詔：中外臣庶之家，子弟或有乖檢，甚為鄉黨所知，雖加戒勖曾不悛改者，並許本家尊長具名聞，州縣遣吏錮送闕下，當配隸諸處。

translations.literal: Therefore an edict: in civil and military households if sons or younger brothers are undisciplined and known to the community though admonished they do not reform, the family elders may report by name; prefectures and counties shall send officers to escort to court and assign to service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: if household sons are undisciplined and known though admonished they do not reform, elders may report them; counties shall escort them to court for assignment.

sentences.zh: 敢有藏匿不以名聞者，異時醜狀彰露，期功以上悉以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Whoever dares conceal and not report—when later their ugliness is exposed—all within mourning of one degree shall be punished for their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever conceals them—when guilt is later exposed—all within one degree of mourning shall be punished.

sentences.zh: 文裕後遷軍器庫使。

translations.literal: Later Wenyu was promoted Arsenal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenyu was promoted Arsenal Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕征太原，命文裕與通事舍人王侁分兵控石嶺關。

translations.literal: In the fourth year when the imperial carriage campaigned at Taiyuan Wenyu was ordered with Communications Officer Wang You to divide troops and control Shiling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 on the Taiyuan campaign Wenyu with Wang You divided troops to hold Shiling Pass.

sentences.zh: 六年，領儒州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he held Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he held Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，為高陽關都監。

translations.literal: The next year he was supreme commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was supreme commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 會契丹萬餘騎入，文裕與大將崔彥進擊卻之。

translations.literal: When over ten thousand Khitan horsemen entered Wenyu with Grand General Cui Yanjin drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When over ten thousand Khitan horsemen entered Wenyu with Cui Yanjin drove them back.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，徙屯三交，加領順州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was moved to station at Sanjiao and was also given regimental command of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxi's start he moved to Sanjiao and was given regimental command of Shun.

sentences.zh: 會李繼遷率折遇乜寇邊，初詔田仁朗與王侁等討之，仁朗坐逗遛，命文裕代仁朗。

translations.literal: When Li Jiyuan with Zheyu Nie raided the border at first Tian Renlang with Wang You and others were ordered to attack; Renlang was punished for delay and Wenyu was ordered to replace Renlang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiyuan with Zheyu Nie raided, Tian Renlang was first ordered to attack; Renlang was punished for delay and Wenyu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 繼遷等遁去。

translations.literal: Jiyuan and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan and the others fled.

sentences.zh: 劉美字世濟，并州人。

translations.literal: Liu Mei, style name Shiji, was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mei, style Shiji, was from Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四世祖質，絳州刺史。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Zhi was prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Zhi was prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖維嶽，不仕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Weiyue did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Weiyue did not serve.

sentences.zh: 祖延慶，右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanqing was General of the Right Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yanqing was General of the Right Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 父通，宋初掌禁旅，從潘美征廣南，又累戰北面，積勞至虎捷都指揮使，領嘉州刺史，太平興國中，扈蹕太原，卒於師，贈潁州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Tong in early Song commanded the palace guard; following Pan Mei he campaigned in Guangnan and fought repeatedly on the northern front; accumulated merit to commander of the Tiger Swift and prefect of Jia; in Taiping Xingguo he escorted the emperor to Taiyuan and died on campaign; posthumously made defender of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Father Tong in early Song commanded palace guard; followed Pan Mei to Guangnan and fought north repeatedly; rose to Tiger Swift commander and Jia prefect; on Taiyuan campaign died; posthumously defender of Ying.
